cs.t: I've built tons of things. Most usefully, I built presence/motion/light/temperature sensors for my home, along with IR transmitter so I can control my TV/AC. They're about the size of two matchboxes, they cost about $10 each and they're amazing for my home automation:  https://gitlab.com/stavros/sensor-board/  I've built cat toys for my blind cat, toy planes, a CNC, a cat feeder, a back-scratching robot, and more stuff that I can't remember. I love the ESP8266. Also, an e-ink display that shows my calendar:  https://www.stavros.io/posts/making-the-timeframe/  A house with a tiny person living in it:  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1RUqTN-7_gU  A way to project images in mid-air, for long exposure photography:  https://www.stavros.io/posts/behold-ledonardo/  A button that I can press to get food:  https://www.stavros.io/posts/emergency-food-button/  A drone that blows bubbles:  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xk99zrlAp9U  A toy bus that shows you when the next actual bus will come:  https://www.stavros.io/posts/bus-stop-bus/  A rotary mobile phone:  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fSkdWQswpc8  An alarm clock with the weather so I know whether it's worth waking up for tennis:  https://www.stavros.io/posts/do-not-be-alarmed-clock/

cs.t: I've been using an ESP8266 as a wifi/modem adapter with my original Commodore 64.  Works really well!  You may be able to get away with something cheaper if you push.  http://tech.guitarsite.de/c64_wifimodem.html
